seo.title: Query a Beancount ledger with SQL on {devices}
seo.description: Open a Beancount ledger as read-only SQL tables of transactions, postings, balances and metadata, follow its includes, and run BQL through rledger.

og.title: Query a Beancount ledger with SQL

header.title: Query a Beancount ledger with SQL on {devices}
header.lead: Open a .beancount file and query its transactions, postings, balances and metadata as SQL tables, or send BQL to rledger. The ledger stays a text file that you edit in your own editor.

sections.title: Open a ledger
paragraphs: TablePro runs rledger or Python Beancount to read the ledger. If you are choosing one, install rledger: it wins when both are present, BQL runs through it alone, and only it fills the diagnostics table with validation output.

Choose the file with Browse… in the connection form. The ledger path is the whole connection, with no host, port, password or database. A .beancount file also opens from Finder, and beancount:///path/to/main.beancount URLs import.

An app opened from Finder does not inherit your shell’s PATH. If the backend runs in Terminal but not here, name it with launchctl setenv TABLEPRO_RUSTLEDGER_BINARY or TABLEPRO_BEANCOUNT_PYTHON and relaunch.

The Python backend runs the plugins that ship with Beancount and skips any other plugin directive, which is third-party code, until you turn on Run Ledger Plugins for that connection. Skipped plugins are listed in diagnostics.

sections.title: Query the ledger
paragraphs: The tables cover transactions and postings, accounts, balances and balance assertions, prices and commodities, every other directive, metadata, tags and links, and the source files. Postings join transactions on transaction_id, and accounts join by name.

Amounts arrive booked, with arithmetic, costs and prices resolved, and posting costs and inline prices in columns of their own. Transactions, postings and several directive tables carry a source_location such as main.beancount:42, so a row leads back to its line.
Prefix a query with BQL: to send it to rledger instead of the tables. Browsing, row counts and paging work on a BQL result; SQL parameters do not.

include directives are followed, literal paths and globs alike, and every ledger file and referenced document is watched. Save a change in your editor and the next query reads it without reconnecting. The connection is always at Safe Mode Read-Only, so INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and schema changes are refused.

sections.title: Move data
paragraphs: Export a table or a query result as {exportFormats}. <files>Other files TablePro opens as databases</files> include SQLite, DuckDB and Parquet.

faq.question: Does a ledger with errors still open?
faq.answer: Through rledger, yes. The ledger is projected even when validation fails, and each problem is a row in diagnostics with its file, line, severity and message.

faq.question: Can one connection open several ledgers?
faq.answer: One connection is one ledger file, with no switching. A main file that includes the others brings them all in, globs included.
